NDT training in Richland: how it works for Richland employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training for Richland and Tri-Cities employers and technicians in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET at Level I, II and III. Theory runs live online, and practical training runs onsite at your facility under ASNT Level III oversight. Certification is issued by your employer under its written practice once you have completed classroom training, documented experience, the exams and a vision test. Nuclear site requirements are layered on top by the site contractor.

Richland is not a typical NDT market. Most US inspection towns are built around a refinery, a shipyard or an aircraft plant. Richland is built around the Hanford Site and the nuclear economy that has grown up beside it. That shapes everything about how NDT technicians are trained, qualified and put to work here. Almost every serious employer runs under a nuclear quality-assurance programme. Many roles need a Department of Energy security clearance. Method certification is necessary but never enough on its own: site procedures, facility-specific training and quality-programme requirements all sit above it. A technician who arrives with a solid SNT-TC-1A certification and no idea how an NQA-1 programme treats records, procedures and nonconformances will find the first months hard.

So the question people in Richland ask is rarely just how to get a UT certificate. It is more often which parts of a nuclear contractor's qualification package are method training they can get outside, and which parts only the site can give. Atlantis NDT covers the first part. We provide formal method training and exam preparation under SNT-TC-1A, and Level III services for employers that need a written practice or outside exam administration. The site contractor provides the site-specific training, facility access, radiological worker qualification and clearance processing. Keeping the two separate, and knowing which is which, saves both employers and technicians a lot of wasted effort.

We are also clear about scope. Atlantis NDT trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A only. Nuclear power plant in-service inspection under ASME Section XI generally uses ANSI/ASNT CP-189 personnel qualification. UT on certain nuclear piping also needs Section XI Appendix VIII performance demonstration. Some Tri-Cities employers ask for AWS CWI, API credentials or ISO 9712. Those are separate schemes, and we do not train or certify to them. Our training gives technicians the method knowledge those schemes build on. If you need to work out which scheme a specific job needs, ask us before you commit to a course.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Richland

All the methods below are available to Richland and Tri-Cities employers and technicians. They are delivered as live-virtual classroom theory, onsite cohorts at your facility, or a blend of both. Course content follows the SNT-TC-1A body of knowledge and the employer's written practice. Practical work uses real specimens. Required classroom and experience hours vary by method, level and written practice, so see the training requirements matrix for recommended figures.

MethodLevelsWhat Richland employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, IIIWall-thickness and weld examination on waste-transfer piping, tank and vessel integrity programmes, fabrication weld inspection on new process equipment, and hydro-structure and penstock thickness surveysLevel I: employer-defined education plus method training. Level II: Level I experience per the written practice
Phased Array UT (PAUT)I, II (Level III through UT)Encoded weld and corrosion examinations where a permanent, reviewable data record is needed, which fits nuclear QA record expectations, and remotely deployed or restricted-access scanning where dose or access limits scan timeUT Level II strongly recommended
Time of Flight Diffraction (TOFD)I, II (Level III through UT)Thick-section welds on vessels and heavy fabrications, and through-wall sizing to support fitness-for-service and engineering evaluationUT Level II strongly recommended
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, IIIWeld radiography on new-construction piping and components, film and digital interpretation for fabrication vendors, and outage piping work at the commercial power stationRadiation-safety training under the licensee's or site's programme, plus RT method training
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, IIISurface crack detection on carbon-steel welds, lifting equipment, structural steel and dam hardwareMethod training and a vision test
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, IIIStainless-steel welds and components, which are very common in nuclear process systems, plus fuel-fabrication and laboratory equipment, and food-processing stainless in the Columbia BasinMethod training and a vision test
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, IIIWeld visual on everything, remote visual inspection with cameras and crawlers where personnel access is limited, and structural and coating condition assessmentMethod training and a vision test (near vision and colour contrast)
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, IIIHeat-exchanger and condenser tube inspection at power generation facilities, surface examination of non-ferrous parts, and conductivity and coating measurementsBasic electricity and magnetism, and method training

Two things are different about the method mix in Richland. First, stainless steel is everywhere in nuclear process systems, so PT and VT carry more weight than in a carbon-steel refinery town. UT on austenitic welds is also harder than UT on carbon steel. Coarse-grained stainless weld metal scatters and redirects sound, and technicians need specific training and technique development to handle it. Second, remote examination is routine. Crawlers, cameras and deployed probes are used wherever dose, contamination or physical access rules out a person with a hand-held probe. Remote visual and encoded UT skills are worth more here than almost anywhere else.

For technicians moving toward Level III, Atlantis NDT offers ASNT Level III exam preparation for the Basic exam and method exams, delivered online. In a quality-driven market like Richland, a Level III who can write a procedure that survives a nuclear QA audit is especially valuable.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Richland, step by step

The core path is the SNT-TC-1A path. Nuclear employers add steps around it, which are noted below.

  1. Your employer's written practice. The written practice defines how the employer trains, examines and certifies NDT personnel. It covers hours, exams, grading, vision testing, recertification and the responsible Level III. In a nuclear QA environment, the written practice is itself a controlled document inside the quality programme, and changes to it are managed formally. See written-practice development.
  2. Formal classroom training. Method training delivered live-virtual, onsite or blended. The hours come from the written practice. Recommended figures are in the training requirements matrix. Keep training records traceable, because nuclear QA auditors will check them.
  3. On-the-job experience. Supervised experience in the method on real work. On a nuclear site this often builds up more slowly than in commercial work, because of access, work-control and radiological constraints, so plan for it.
  4. General examination. A written exam on the principles of the method.
  5. Specific examination. A written exam on the employer's procedures, codes and equipment. In Richland this can include nuclear quality requirements, ASME code sections and site-specific procedures.
  6. Practical examination. Hands-on examination of real specimens with real discontinuities, performed and documented to procedure, administered by a Level III or designated examiner.
  7. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour-contrast testing per the written practice, repeated annually.
  8. Certification by the employer. The employer certifies you for the method and level, with the full record on file.
  9. Site-specific qualification. This is not part of SNT-TC-1A itself, but it is essential here. The site contractor adds facility training, radiological worker training, work-control qualification and, for most roles, clearance. You can only do NDT on the site once these are complete.
  10. Recertification. On the interval set by the written practice. Certification generally ends when you leave an employer, and a new employer re-certifies you under its own written practice.

Our SNT-TC-1A training and certification guide explains the employer-based model in more depth.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Richland crews

Atlantis NDT has no physical training centre in Richland or anywhere else. For Tri-Cities employers, training is delivered in three ways.

Live-virtual classroom. Instructor-led theory online, with real-time questions and exercises. This suits Richland well. Getting people off a controlled site for a week of classroom time is expensive, and online theory can be spread across shifts. See online NDT training.

Onsite at your facility. An ASNT Level III-led instructor comes to your facility for practical training and the practical exam, bringing reference specimens or using yours. On a controlled nuclear site, the realistic setting is usually the contractor's own offices or shops in Richland, outside the controlled area, because instructor access to controlled areas takes time to arrange. Your Level III can also hold practical exams there on representative specimens.

Blended. Theory online, practical onsite. For most Richland employers this is the right balance between cost, time off the job and hands-on quality.

Scheduling follows the site's rhythms: fiscal-year funding cycles, work-control windows and, at the commercial nuclear station, refuelling outages on a two-year cycle, during which almost nobody can be spared for training. We schedule cohorts before or after those peaks. Ask about onsite training for your Richland crew, and we will send cohort and onsite quotes within one business day. Multi-method or multi-year programmes run through our corporate NDT training service.

Where NDT technicians work in Richland

The Hanford Site. Hanford is one of the largest environmental cleanup projects in the world. It is the legacy of decades of plutonium production, including roughly 56 million gallons of radioactive and hazardous waste held in 177 underground tanks. The cleanup mission creates NDT work in several forms. The tank farms run integrity programmes, including ultrasonic examination of double-shell tank walls with remotely deployed equipment. Waste-transfer lines and process piping need thickness and weld examination. Legacy facilities under demolition and decommissioning need structural and component assessments. Each of these runs under nuclear quality-assurance requirements, with NQA-1-based programmes and DOE nuclear-safety rules, and most roles need a DOE clearance.

The Waste Treatment and Immobilization Plant. In October 2025, after decades of design and construction, the Waste Treatment and Immobilization Plant began vitrifying tank waste in its Low-Activity Waste Facility. The facility combines waste with glass-forming materials in large melters and pours the result into stainless-steel containers. The plant's move from construction into operation shifts NDT demand. Weld inspection on new construction gives way to in-service examination, maintenance and repair of stainless process systems, melters, piping and containers, where PT, VT, UT and remote examination all apply.

Commercial nuclear power. Columbia Generating Station, operated by Energy Northwest on the Hanford Site north of Richland, is the Northwest's only commercial nuclear power plant. Its refuelling outages bring surges of in-service inspection work. As noted above, nuclear plant in-service inspection under ASME Section XI generally uses CP-189 personnel qualification, not SNT-TC-1A, and nuclear piping UT needs performance demonstration on top. Atlantis NDT's SNT-TC-1A training gives the method grounding, but it is not a substitute for those qualifications. Outage vendors and utilities handle them through their own programmes.

Research and fuel manufacturing. Pacific Northwest National Laboratory, operated by Battelle in Richland, is a major Department of Energy research laboratory with a large engineering and fabrication support base. Framatome runs a nuclear fuel fabrication plant in Richland. Both need NDT on components, pressure equipment and fabricated hardware, usually with an emphasis on stainless steel and precision work, and usually under formal quality programmes.

Hydroelectric and regional industry. The Columbia and Snake River dams around the Tri-Cities, including Ice Harbor and McNary, need periodic inspection of penstocks, gates, cranes and structural steel, with UT thickness surveys, MT and VT the main methods. Across the Columbia Basin, food processing, fertiliser and agricultural industry operate boilers, pressure vessels and stainless process equipment that need routine NDT. Steel fabrication shops in Pasco and Kennewick supply the region's energy and construction work to codes such as AWS D1.1 and ASME Section VIII.

Codes and quality frameworks. Across the Richland market you will see ASME NQA-1 quality assurance, DOE nuclear-safety rules (10 CFR 830) and occupational radiation protection (10 CFR 835), ASME Section III for nuclear construction, ASME Section XI for in-service inspection at the power station, ASME B31.3 for process piping, ASME Section VIII for pressure vessels and AWS D1.1 for structural steel. You do not need to memorise all of them before you start. But technicians who understand how a procedure traces back to a code, and how a record traces back to a procedure, progress fastest.

Radiography licensing. Washington is an NRC Agreement State. The Washington State Department of Health's Office of Radiation Protection licenses radioactive-material use in the state, including industrial radiography, and registers x-ray equipment. Its industrial radiography rules follow the federal Part 34 model, requiring approved training programmes and recognised radiation-safety qualification for radiographers on top of SNT-TC-1A RT method certification. Work inside DOE facilities is also governed by DOE's own radiation-protection rules and site procedures. RT crews should confirm with the site contractor exactly which requirements apply before mobilising. For pay context, see our NDT salary guide. We do not publish local salary figures on this page.

Level III services and written practices for Richland NDT companies

In a nuclear QA market, the paperwork is part of the product. A subcontractor that performs good examinations but cannot show a controlled written practice, traceable training records, current vision tests and exam records signed by a responsible Level III will fail supplier audits, however skilled its technicians are. Richland employers typically need:

  • A written practice written for a quality-programme environment: precise about responsibilities, controlled revisions and record retention, and consistent with the employer's QA manual. See written-practice development.
  • A responsible Level III for procedure approval, exam administration and certification sign-off. Many smaller Tri-Cities firms use an outside Level III under a services agreement, which SNT-TC-1A allows.
  • Procedure writing and review, especially for stainless-steel UT, remote visual examination and encoded PAUT, where generic procedures do not hold up.
  • Certification-file audits before a customer or regulator audit, to find gaps while there is still time to close them.

Atlantis NDT provides these Level III services remotely, with onsite visits where needed. The SNT-TC-1A guidance page covers the framework. Book a Level III consultation to review your programme or plan an audit response.

Practise before the practical exam

Practical exams are where theory meets hands. Candidates who know the material still lose marks on calibration sequence, coverage, indication evaluation and reporting. Atlantis NDT's Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees rehearse 12 NDT methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Richland technicians, the NDT lab and storage tank environments are the closest match to tank-integrity and component examination work.

The simulator is for practice only. It does not replace the practical examination, which under SNT-TC-1A must be done on real specimens with real discontinuities using actual equipment, graded by a Level III or designated examiner. Use it to rehearse. Then prove it on real parts. For the written exams, work through our UT Level 2 practice questions and similar mock exams.

Your instructor

Atlantis NDT training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. Anoop sets the course content, oversees onsite and live-virtual delivery, and provides Level III oversight for employers who use Atlantis NDT's Level III services. See the full NDT training catalogue for every method and level.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Richland

How do I get NDT certified in Richland?

Under ASNT SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you after you complete formal method training, log on-the-job experience, pass general, specific and practical exams administered by a Level III, and pass a vision test. On the Hanford Site and at nuclear employers, site-specific training and, for most roles, a DOE clearance come on top of method certification.

Can I take NDT training online in Washington State?

Yes. Method theory runs as live-virtual classroom sessions you can join from Richland or anywhere in Washington. The practical portion and practical exam need hands-on work with real specimens, and Atlantis NDT delivers that onsite at your employer's facility. No legitimate SNT-TC-1A certification is completed entirely online.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It depends on the classroom hours in your employer's written practice, the on-the-job experience you must log and your exam schedule. Classroom time is the quick part. Experience hours take longest, and on nuclear sites access constraints can slow them down further. See the training requirements matrix for recommended figures.

Do I need a license for radiography in Washington State?

The license belongs to the company. Companies doing industrial radiography with radioactive sources in Washington need a license from the Department of Health's Office of Radiation Protection, and x-ray equipment must be registered. Individual radiographers need recognised radiation-safety qualification under the licensee's programme, as well as SNT-TC-1A RT certification. Inside DOE facilities, DOE radiation-protection rules and site procedures also apply.

What does NDT training cost in Richland?

Pricing is quote on request. It depends on method, level, group size, onsite versus online delivery and any Level III services you need. We send cohort and onsite quotes within one business day. Request a Richland training quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Richland employers?

SNT-TC-1A is widely used by DOE contractors, fabricators and vendors in the Tri-Cities, usually inside an NQA-1 quality programme. Nuclear power plant in-service inspection generally uses ANSI/ASNT CP-189 instead, with performance demonstration for certain UT examinations. Because certification is employer-based, a new employer re-certifies you under its own written practice.

Does your training qualify me for work at Columbia Generating Station?

Not on its own. Nuclear plant in-service inspection under ASME Section XI generally needs CP-189 personnel qualification, and UT on certain components needs Appendix VIII performance demonstration, both handled through the utility's or outage vendor's programme. Our SNT-TC-1A training builds the method foundation those qualifications rest on.

Do I need a security clearance to do NDT at Hanford?

Most roles on the Hanford Site need a DOE clearance, processed through the employing contractor. Atlantis NDT does not process clearances. Clearance processing can take a long time, so employers usually start it early and use the waiting period for method training and certification.

Why is stainless-steel UT treated as a special skill in Richland?

Austenitic stainless weld metal has a coarse, directional grain structure that scatters and bends ultrasound, producing noise and misleading indications. Nuclear process systems use a lot of it. Technicians need specific technique training, suitable probes and procedures qualified for the material, which is why general carbon-steel UT experience does not transfer automatically.

Can you train our team at our Richland office instead of on the site?

Yes, and for most Hanford contractors that is the practical choice. Onsite training can run at your Richland offices or shops outside controlled areas, with theory online beforehand, which avoids the time needed to arrange instructor access to controlled areas.

We need a written practice that will pass a nuclear QA audit. Can you help?

Yes. Atlantis NDT develops written practices and procedures for quality-programme environments and can serve as your outside Level III. Book a Level III consultation to scope the work.

Do you offer Level III exam preparation for Tri-Cities technicians?

Yes. Our ASNT Level III exam preparation covers the Basic exam and method exams and is delivered live online, so Richland, Kennewick and Pasco candidates can prepare without travelling.
